svg.text: Humble Object pattern: split behaviour into two modules, a humble one with the hard-to-test behaviour stripped to its barest essence and another with all the testable
behaviour taken out of it; it helps find and protect architectural boundaries
Application
Date, Currency objects
Presenter (testable)
formats into Strings, booleans, enums
View (humble)
moves ViewModel data onto the screen
View Model: a simple data structure holding everything on screen that the application controls, as Strings, booleans or enums: a formatted date, money with decimals and
currency marker plus a boolean to turn negative values red, button and menu names with grey-out flags, radio button, check box and text field names, tables of formatted
strings. The View does nothing but load it into the screen. GUIs are hard to unit test because tests cannot easily see the screen, but most GUI behaviour is easy to
test once separated.
Database gateways (Fowler)
polymorphic interfaces with a method per create, read, update or delete the
application needs (UserGateway.getLastNamesOfUsersWhoLoggedInAfter(Date)); no SQL
in the use cases: implementations in the database layer are the humble objects;
interactors are not humble but testable with stubs or test doubles
Data mappers, service listeners
'ORM' is a misnomer: objects hide data and expose operations, data structures
expose data with no behaviour; mappers load data into data structures, a Humble
Object boundary in the database layer; services: load simple structures, humble
modules format and send; listeners turn input into simple structures
